claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers is primarily governed by dislocation accumulation and transmission at nanoscale interfaces.
Compositional complexity and severe lattice distortion cause the multilayer interfaces to act as dislocation barriers.
Dislocation barriers at the interfaces promote local dislocation pile-up.
Interface pile-ups produce local stress concentrations that activate non-basal slip or deformation twinning above a critical stress.
The starting coatings consist of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers with coherent or semi-coherent interfaces.
The starting multilayers exhibit significant compositional complexity and lattice distortion.
Room or moderately elevated temperatures avoid thermally activated extraneous diffusion effects during the proposed creep test.
Under sustained stress, dislocations nucleate and move within the individual FCC and BCC layers.
Dislocations moving within the layers are impeded when they reach the FCC/BCC interfaces.
Interface pile-ups raise local stresses until secondary deformation mechanisms accommodate further plastic flow.
Severe lattice distortion accentuates the proposed change in deformation mode by promoting dislocation nucleation while impeding long-range glide.
Short-range ordering in the high-entropy alloy accentuates the interface-mediated deformation process.
Sustained loading will produce significant dislocation pile-ups at multilayer interfaces relative to the starting state.
The active deformation mode will shift from conventional slip toward non-basal slip or twinning.
The creep rate will measurably increase over time as interface pile-ups and alternative deformation mechanisms develop.
Dislocation pile-up, alternative slip or twinning, and creep-rate acceleration will be more pronounced at intentionally less coherent or more distorted interfaces.
The proposed mechanism is dominant only when applied stress exceeds the level required for significant dislocation accumulation at nanoscale interfaces.
The proposed mechanism requires retention of the nanoscale interface structure without complete interdiffusion or coarsening.
Conventional multilayers lacking pronounced compositional complexity and lattice distortion may not exhibit the same deformation progression.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as undeformed while also stating that dislocation motion occurs by conventional slip; the predicted-outcome field additionally assumes an initial homogeneous dislocation distribution. An undeformed state does not itself exhibit active dislocation motion, and the homogeneous starting distribution is not established elsewhere.
